crime: Trimming her little sister's fringe at the kitchen table, {WITCH_NAME} pictured closing the scissors on that small throat. Her hand stopped. Her mother took them: "What's wrong with your face?" After that she smiled at everyone. Such a girl must never be looked at closely.

Every Sunday a prisoner cut the girls' hair on a stool in the courtyard, as she had for her little brother. In her apron, she pinned a white cape at each girl's throat. {WITCH_NAME} always smiled and declined her turn.

One Sunday the barber gave her the scissors and tipped her own head back: "Your turn. An inch off my fringe." She stopped, blades open at the barber's throat. The barber laughed to the waiting line: "She's shaking! From now on she does my fringe every Sunday till her hands are steady." Every girl looked at those hands.

When the others went in, she asked to try the fringe again and drove the scissors into the barber's side under the apron. The barber met her smile; her Magic loosened her shoulders. "It's only a nick." The barber pocketed her scissors and followed {WITCH_NAME} in.
In the lounge the barber sat quiet by her until lockup; each time she looked up, {WITCH_NAME} was smiling. Nobody noticed.
At lockup the barber hung her apron outside her barred cell door to keep hair out. She called goodnight across the cell corridor to the smiling {WITCH_NAME} and took her scissors in.
Her roommate woke to find her dead in a blood-soaked blanket, the scissors bloody on the floor. The prisoners blamed the roommate, locked in with her all night.

But that morning a prisoner had turned over the apron on the door: a slit in its side, dried blood inside. Now the prisoners saw: the barber, stabbed through it before lockup, said goodnight calmly because {WITCH_NAME} smiled at her all evening.
fields.epitaph: Her hands were only ever steady when it was real.
fields.epithet: A Steady Smile Over a Shaking Hand
execution: The execution stand raises a tall haircut stool into the trial court. She is strapped to its seat, a white cape pinned at her throat and its hem pinned to the floor all the way round.
The stool rises slowly. The cape draws taut from floor to throat, and its collar tightens.
As the collar tightens, she smiles at the spectators. Their faces soften and their shoulders loosen, at ease.
The stool stops high above the court. The cape is a still white tent from her throat to the floor, and the spectators sit at ease.

magic.name: All Is Well
magic.text: Any person or animal whose eyes meet her smile is instantly flooded with calm, sure that all is well.
